subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 30-year-old woman is evaluated because her 58-year-old father has end-stage renal disease, angiokeratomas, and a history of painful hands and feet; her 27-year-old brother has similar skin lesions and proteinuria. She has mild proteinuria and is otherwise asymptomatic.
question: Which of the following patterns of inheritance best fits the condition in this family?
explanation_correct: Fabry disease is an X-linked recessive disorder caused by alpha-galactosidase A deficiency, so an affected father transmits the variant to all of his daughters, who become carriers. Skewed X-inactivation can make carrier females symptomatic, explaining this woman's mild proteinuria while her male relatives have severe disease. Affected males do not transmit the disorder to their sons.

explanation_incorrect.A: An autosomal dominant pattern would not explain the severe male-predominant disease with only mild findings in the daughter.
explanation_incorrect.B: Autosomal recessive disease requires two carrier parents and affects males and females equally.
explanation_incorrect.C: In X-linked dominant disease all daughters of an affected father are affected, usually with substantial disease, which does not fit this carrier state.
explanation_incorrect.D: Mitochondrial inheritance is strictly maternal, but this trait came through the father.

educationalObjective: Fabry disease is X-linked recessive, so affected fathers pass the variant to all daughters, who may show mild disease from skewed X-inactivation.
